p1_h: Audio becomes text on your Mac
p1_p: Recordings and meeting records stay on your own disk. The only things sent out are the recognized text (for translation and notes) and, when you use interpreting, the few sentences you speak while holding the key.

faq: Will it run on my Mac?

You need macOS 14.4 or later on an Apple silicon Mac. macOS 26 uses the newer on-device speech recognizer, the most accurate; 14.4 to 15 use the system's earlier one, a little weaker, which needs Dictation turned on in System Settings › Keyboard, with each language you want heard added to it.

Cicada is free and open source. Live subtitles, translation and meeting records work without a key. AI notes and natural voices use your own Ling key: about ¥0.15–1 per hour of meeting, and Ling gives ¥10 of credit every month.
No bot joins the call, and nobody else installs anything. When you share your screen, the notes window stays out of the picture by default.
Audio turns into text on your Mac, and recordings stay there. Only the recognized text leaves it, plus the few sentences you say while holding the talk key for interpreting.

It detects the language being spoken, among those your Mac’s on-device speech recognition supports, and translates into your system language by default. Natural interpreting voices cover English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, German, French and Spanish.
Is what I say out loud recorded?
For now, only what you say while holding the talk key. “Record what I say” is first on the roadmap.
macOS blocked it on first launch?
Cicada isn’t notarized by Apple yet. Go to System Settings › Privacy & Security and click “Open Anyway”, once. Proper signing is on the roadmap.
A virtual microphone, BlackHole. The first time you turn on interpreting, Cicada downloads it from the official source, installs it and runs a sound check.
